entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Old-fashioned and slightly fond, as of children.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Nearly neutral, and the only word that lets the winning be the point rather than the gloating.

entries.definition: worn away as by water or ice or wind
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Worn by water or wind, and the same word means thoroughly cleaned.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The superlative - courage as legend.

entries.definition: devouring or craving food in great quantities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Predatory and archaic-sounding, as of a beast that has not eaten.

entries.definition: having or showing arrogant superiority to and disdain of those one views as unworthy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Superiority that pushes other people around.

entries.definition: refined and tasteful in appearance or behavior or style
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Restraint doing the work - the highest praise in the family, and the quietest.

entries.definition: subdued or brought low in condition or status
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Requires an audience - the lowering had to be seen to count.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British, and it makes the complaining sound wet and wearing.

entries.definition: marked by or given to doubt
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The British spelling, identical in force.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Old and severe: it implies a standard has been abandoned, not merely missed.

entries.definition: in an overbearingly domineering manner; as a dictator
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *dictatorial*: borrows a form of government to describe a manner; the comparison is the insult.
examples: this manager acts dictatorially toward his colleagues

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cooler and more measured; it values the thing rather than feeling the debt.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: American and dismissive - *a bum deal*, *a bum knee*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *angry*: reports the feeling without judging it; the mildest and least loaded word in the family.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Brisk and a little relentless - it can condescend when said of an adult.
examples: a perky little widow in her 70s

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *vicious*: adds enjoyment to the harm - a vicious act is one the doer wanted to do.

entries.definition: showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and settled - a disposition rather than a mood, which is why institutions claim it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faintly mocking - the sentimentality is being pointed at.

entries.definition: noisily domineering; tending to browbeat others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Noise without much force behind it; more ridiculous than frightening.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and withering - sweetness pushed past charm into embarrassment.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *boastful*: faults the telling rather than the feeling - pride said out loud too often.

entries.definition: subdued or brought low in condition or status
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest word here, and always about defeat rather than character.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Repetition is the offence: the complaint is not wrong, only relentless.
examples: She nags her husband all day long

entries.definition: hasty and without attention to detail; not thorough
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and cool - it reports the shallowness without raising its voice.
examples: a casual (or cursory) inspection failed to reveal the house's structural flaws

entries.definition: in fortunate circumstances financially; moderately rich
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Wealth read as the reward of success - approving.

entries.definition: delighting the senses or exciting intellectual or emotional admiration
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The full word - unreserved and applicable to anything from a face to an argument.

entries.definition: concerned chiefly or only with yourself and your advantage to the exclusion of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same word with an extra syllable, and no extra force.
examples: However, because of their strong-minded nature, they are often perceived as difficult and egoistical individuals.

entries.definition: slow to learn or understand; lacking intellectual acuity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The softened word - avoids naming a deficit outright.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Has moved into politics, where it is about difference rather than difficulty.
examples: injustice can make us tolerant and forgiving

entries.definition: noisy like the sound of a bee
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Low continuous noise as a sign of life - a room abuzz is a room going well.
examples: the room was abuzz over the latest scandal

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Abundance more than kindness - the giving is a matter of plenty.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *haughty*: cold, distant superiority - looking down from a height.
examples: he peered haughtily down his nose

entries.definition: hasty and without attention to detail; not thorough
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Barely a judgement: a passing glance is short, not necessarily careless.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mass theft amid disorder - war, riot, disaster.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Judges the character, not the moment: a person built this way, from the old humours.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Another organ, another temper, and the most literary of the set.

entries.definition: suspicious or unduly suspicious or fearful of being displaced by a rival
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Shakespeare's monster, and the phrase has outlived the play.

entries.definition: make off with belongings of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casual and unserious - petty and quick.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Rude by default in English - the length of the look is what makes it an offence.
examples: The ancestor in the painting is staring down menacingly

entries.definition: appealing to the emotions as well as the eye
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and affectionate - beauty that moves the feelings, not just the eye.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The looking has become thinking - attention paid rather than merely directed.

entries.definition: of a stern or strict bearing or demeanor; forbidding in aspect
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Bare rather than harsh, and in architecture and prose it is often praise.

entries.definition: given to excess in consumption of especially food or drink
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names one of the seven deadly sins; the excess is a moral failure, not an appetite.
examples: over-fed women and their gluttonous husbands

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Frankness without calculation; the opposite of *disingenuous*, which is the commoner word.
examples: his ingenuous explanation that he would not have burned the church if he had not thought the bishop was in it

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Weakened by medicine, where a benign growth is merely not malignant.

entries.definition: (used informally especially for emphasis) real or genuine
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The polite version, with the oath taken out.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *ruthless*: the everyday word, and the one business writing quietly turns into a compliment.
examples: the government has been urged to take immediate action to deal ruthlessly with the strikers
